name: Sticky Feature Story
hint: Scroll: the pinned window turns a recording into notes, tasks, a recap and a search result.
description: A "how it works" section: chapters scroll in one column while a pinned window beside them shows the active one, with a progress rail of chapter ticks. Pass `features` (label, title, body, an optional detail and a visual node each) and the window crossfades between their visuals as the reader scrolls; the rail and the chapter headings jump between chapters. With `demo` it shows a sample story where the window is a single live mock, not a set of images: waveform bars lie down into the words of the notes, sentences lift out as task rows, the rows fly into their owners' avatars and the page folds into a card that ends up as a search result. Scroll position drives it, holding on each chapter and settling on a spring when you stop, and it is fully reversible. It finds its own scroll container, never takes over scrolling, pins to the top of the screen on phones and can show one chapter at a time (`autoplay`) where there is no room to scroll.
intents: how it works section with a sticky product visual that changes as you scroll
scrollytelling feature section for a landing page
pinned product demo with scrolling chapters and a progress rail
explain a product in steps with one animated mockup
usage: Use once on a landing page, after the hero, to walk through how the product works in three to five steps. Pass `features`: each one a short `title`, a two-sentence `body`, a `label` for the rail and a `visual` (any node: an image, a video, a mock) that the pinned window shows while that chapter is active. Read or drive the active chapter with `active` / `defaultActive` / `onActiveChange` (setting `active` scrolls to that chapter). It drives itself from the nearest scrollable ancestor (or the window); pass `scroller` if yours is unusual and `topOffset` for a fixed header. Keep ancestors between it and the scroller free of `overflow: hidden`, which stops the pin. Turn on `autoplay` only where the section cannot scroll, such as a preview card; it advances on a timer only when you set `interval`. Under reduced motion your visuals change by fading, without sliding. With no `features` it shows nothing (or only the header you pass).

dataProps.description: The chapters, in order. `visual` is what the pinned window shows while that chapter is active; `alt` makes the visual one image with that text (leave it out if the visual has its own accessible content). `label` is the short name on the rail and above the title.
